title: Scientists and ethical discipline
competency: Appreciate the work of world and Ethiopian scientists and explain why ethics matter in science.

keywords.def: Someone who gathers evidence in an orderly way, makes hypotheses, tests them, and shares what is learned.
The principles of right and wrong that guide how scientists behave, such as honesty and responsibility.
A substance that kills snails. Endod berries are a strong, cheap and safe molluscicide.

en.text: A scientist gathers evidence in an orderly way, tests ideas and shares knowledge. World scientists include Newton, Curie, Faraday and Einstein. Ethiopian scientists include Dr. Aklilu Lemma, who found that endod kills the snails that spread bilharzia, and Dr. Gebisa Ejeta, known for sorghum.

am.text: ሳይንቲስት ማስረጃን በሥርዓት ይሰበስባል፣ ሐሳቦችን ይፈትሻል፣ እውቀትንም ያካፍላል። የዓለም ሳይንቲስቶች ኒውተን፣ ኩሪ፣ ፋራዴይና አንስታይን ናቸው። ከኢትዮጵያ ሳይንቲስቶች ዶ/ር አክሊሉ ለማ እንዶድ ቢልሃርዝያን የሚያስተላልፉ ቀንድ አውጣዎችን እንደሚገድል አግኝተዋል፤ ዶ/ር ገቢሳ እጀታ በማሽላ ሥራቸው ይታወቃሉ።

screens.title: A plant against disease
screens.text: Bilharzia is a disease spread by a tiny worm. The worm lives part of its life in water snails.
screens.ask: How could a plant help stop bilharzia?
screens.after: An Ethiopian scientist found such a plant: endod. Read on.

screens.title: What is a scientist?
paras: A scientist systematically gathers and uses research and evidence.
A scientist makes hypotheses and tests them. The aim is to gain and share understanding and knowledge.
Here are some world and Ethiopian scientists and what they gave us.

screens.title: Name it
defs: Someone who gathers evidence in an orderly way, makes hypotheses, tests them, and shares what is learned.

screens.title: What scientists do
screens.text: Which of these is the work of a scientist?
opts: Gathering evidence, testing hypotheses and sharing knowledge
screens.ans: Gathering evidence, testing hypotheses and sharing knowledge
screens.why: A scientist gathers evidence, tests hypotheses and shares understanding.

screens.title: World scientists
paras: Marie Curie (1867–1934) won the Nobel Prize for discovering the elements polonium and radium.
Isaac Newton (1643–1727) discovered the laws of motion and the law of gravity.
Michael Faraday (1791–1867) discovered how to make electricity from magnetism. He built the first dynamo.
Albert Einstein (1879–1955) developed the theory of special relativity.
screens.note: Marie Curie won two Nobel Prizes: Physics (1903) and Chemistry (1911).

screens.title: Motion and gravity
screens.text: Which scientist discovered the laws of motion and the law of gravity?
screens.why: Newton (1643–1727) discovered the laws of motion and gravity.
screens.clue: Read the second line of "World scientists".

screens.title: Ethiopian scientists
paras: Dr. Aklilu Lemma (1935–1997) found a natural treatment for schistosomiasis (bilharzia, snail fever) in 1964.
Berries of the endod plant are used for soap and shampoo in many parts of Africa. They are a strong, cheap and safe molluscicide (snail killer). This stops the spread of the parasitic worm.

Prof. Yalemtsehay Mekonnen was born in Asela on 30 May 1955 (as printed). She works on human physiology, the effect of pesticides on health, and plants as medicine for people and animals. She was the first female professor of Addis Ababa University.
Dr. Tewolde Berhan Gebre Egziabher worked to protect biodiversity and the rights of communities to their genetic resources.

Dr. Gebisa Ejeta (born 1950) is a plant breeder and geneticist at Purdue University. He won the World Food Prize in 2009 for his work on sorghum. He helped develop commercial hybrid sorghum for Africa.

screens.title: How endod helps
screens.text: Dr. Aklilu Lemma's endod discovery helps prevent bilharzia.
opts: Endod berries kill the snails that spread the disease
screens.ans: Endod berries kill the snails that spread the disease
screens.why: The berries are a molluscicide: they kill snails, so the parasitic worm cannot spread.
screens.clue: What does a molluscicide kill? (Bilharzia is also called snail fever.)

screens.title: Protecting biodiversity
screens.text: Which Ethiopian scientist worked to protect biodiversity and communities' rights to their genetic resources?
screens.why: That is the work of Dr. Tewolde Berhan Gebre Egziabher.
screens.clue: Compare the Ethiopian scientists in the reading.

screens.title: A prize for food
screens.ask: Dr. Gebisa Ejeta won the World Food Prize in 2009 for his work on ___.
screens.why: He is a plant breeder known for sorghum.
screens.clue: It is a grain crop. In Amharic it is called mashila.
screens.worked: The reading says he won the World Food Prize in 2009 for his contributions to sorghum. He helped develop hybrid sorghum for Africa. So the answer is sorghum.

en.text: Ethics are the principles of right and wrong that guide scientists. They keep science honest, careful and fair, so results can be trusted. Scientific codes address honesty, responsibility, objectivity, openness, competence, legality, non-discrimination and carefulness.

am.text: ሥነ ምግባር ሳይንቲስቶችን የሚመሩ የትክክልና የስሕተት መርሆዎች ናቸው። ሳይንስን ታማኝ፣ ጥንቁቅና ፍትሐዊ ያደርጋሉ፤ ውጤቶችም እንዲታመኑ ያደርጋሉ። ሳይንሳዊ ደንቦች ታማኝነትን፣ ኃላፊነትን፣ ገለልተኝነትን፣ ግልጽነትን፣ ብቃትን፣ ሕጋዊነትን፣ አለማዳላትንና ጥንቃቄን ይመለከታሉ።

screens.title: A different result
screens.text: Your group in the school lab got a result that is different from the book.
screens.ask: What should you write in your report?
screens.after: Honest scientists report what they really found. Read on.

screens.title: Ethical principles in science
paras: Ethics are an essential part of science.
Like science itself, ethics must be consistent and justified when we judge what scientists do.
Things in front of us can be right or wrong, good or bad. We must decide what we really want to do from an ethical point of view.
Scientific codes address these principles: honesty, responsibility, objectivity, openness, competence, legality, non-discrimination and carefulness.

screens.title: What each principle means
paras: Here is a short meaning and a school example for each principle.
table: Tell the truth about your methods and results.
Write the readings you really measured.
Take care for your work and how it affects people and the environment.
Clean up and dispose of waste properly.
Judge by the evidence, not by what you wish were true.
Report a result even if it shows your idea was wrong.
Share your methods and results and listen to others.
Know how to do the work well and keep learning.
Learn how to use an apparatus before you use it.
Follow the rules and laws that apply to your work.
Every member of the group gets a turn.
Work carefully and check your work to avoid mistakes.

screens.title: Name it
defs: The principles of right and wrong that guide how scientists behave, such as honesty and responsibility.

screens.title: Sharing methods
screens.text: A scientist shares her methods so that others can repeat her experiment.
screens.why: Openness means sharing methods and results and listening to others.
screens.clue: Find the principle about sharing in the table.

screens.title: Double-checking
screens.text: A student double-checks every reading before writing it down.
screens.why: Carefulness means working with care and checking to avoid mistakes.
screens.clue: Which principle is about avoiding mistakes?

screens.title: Changing the results
screens.text: Selam's measurements do not match the book. She changes her numbers so they match.
screens.why: Honesty means reporting what really happened, even if it differs from the book.
screens.clue: Which principle is about telling the truth?
screens.ask: Which ethical principle is she breaking?
screens.worked: Selam wrote numbers she did not really measure. Honesty means telling the truth about your results. So she breaks the principle of honesty.

screens.title: Evidence first
screens.ask: Judging by the evidence, not by what you wish were true, is called ___.
screens.why: Objectivity means judging by the evidence.
screens.clue: Look at the third row of the table.
